card.name: Start of split drug and medical terms
card.fires_on: The first piece of a word that is split up, right after a boundary such as a comma, hyphen, slash or the word 'or'. It is usually a brand name (Avastin, Renflexis, Avodart) or a term like monotherapy, radiological or rheumatology.

modes.label: monotherapy
modes.description: The opening piece of 'monotherapy' in dosing tables and regimen text.
modes.example: Dosing recommendations for monotherapy or<< mon>>otherapy following intravenous nivolumab

modes.label: Brand names
modes.description: The opening piece of a brand-name drug, often at the start of a sentence or in parentheses.
modes.example: No dose reductions for<< Av>>astin are recommended.

modes.label: Medical terms
modes.description: The opening piece of a long clinical word after a bracket, hyphen or abbreviation.

card.writes: The promoted tokens are unrelated, so there is no clear output effect; it mildly suppresses 'agent' and 'efficacy' words.
card.plain: It fires on the first chunk of a long drug name or medical term that the model sees in pieces.
